sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the building of Malchus requires a drawing down from the essence of Ein Sof, because Malchus is the power of revelation, and on Rosh Hashanah this revelation must extend even into inanimate physical existence.

translations.translation: d)
And elsewhere,31
the reason for this is explained—that in order for the building of Malchus to occur, it must be through a drawing down from the essence of Ein Sof,
for Malchus is the matter of revelation.
And even the Malchus within each Sefirah is the power of revelation of that Sefirah.32
However, the revelation through the Malchus of the Sefiros is in Atzilus,33
and in order for there to be revelation in Biyah, it is through Malchus as a separate Partzuf.
This is analogous to speech in a person
(Malchus is the matter of speech,
Malchus of the mouth34)
which is revelation to another.
And the matter of the building of Malchus on Rosh Hashanah is,35
that the revelation should be not only in the spiritual creations of Biyah, but also in physical Asiyah,
and within this itself—to the lowest level,
even to the inanimate,
as we say in the Rosh Hashanah prayers, "And every formed being shall know that You formed it,"
so that even the inanimate
(which is in Asiyah)36
shall know that You formed it.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the coronation on Rosh Hashanah requires the physical act of shofar blowing, specifically with a detached horn, to draw revelation down to the inanimate level and the animal within man.

translations.translation: And this is the meaning of the statement, "Recite before Me the verses of Kingship, so that you make Me King over you... and with what? With the shofar."
Among the reasons for this—that reciting the Kingship verses is insufficient and one must also blow the shofar—
is,37
that the matter of "you shall make Me King" on Rosh Hashanah is that the revelation be drawn into Asiyah,
and this is accomplished through the physical act of blowing the shofar.
And through the fact that the act of blowing the shofar is that one blows into a shofar from an animal,
the revelation is drawn also into physical matters,
the animal within man.
And in order for the revelation to be drawn further downward, even to the inanimate,
the shofar horn that one blows must be detached
(and not attached to the animal),
inanimate.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the lower the descent of the drawing down, the higher its source must be, illustrated by the power of abstraction in Chochmah, where clothing the intellect in a parable paradoxically reveals the essence of abstraction.

translations.translation: Now, the more the drawing down is to a lower level,
the more it is through the source of the drawing down being higher.
And as brought38
the analogy for this from the power of abstraction in Chochmah,
the descent is according to the manner of abstraction.
For in order to bring down the intellect and clothe it in a parable
(and that the parable be precise),
it is specifically when one knows the essence of the matter.
And to note,
that in the power of descent of the intellect there are two matters.
That it is able to contract the intellect to be commensurate with the student,
and that it is able to conceal the intellect by clothing it in a parable.
And even to contract the intellect requires a higher power.
And it can be said,
that the reason the maamar brings the matter of the descent of clothing in a parable,
is,
because it speaks here of the power of abstraction
(abstraction)
that is in Chochmah,
and regarding this matter, the descent of clothing in a parable is more relevant.
For although the matter of clothing in a parable
(unlike the descent of contraction)
is seemingly the opposite of the matter of abstraction,
nevertheless,
in that one clothes the intellect in a parable, the power of abstraction of Chochmah is recognized and revealed.
For that clothing in a parable is the opposite of abstraction is when the abstraction is defined and imagined in the conception of being above clothing in a parable,
but from the perspective of the true essence of abstraction,
clothing in a parable is also possible.
